cards.label: Shoreditch - a service yard behind a coffee place
cards.text: Des has brought you to the least interesting place in Shoreditch and is looking at it with open enthusiasm.

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "Everyone looks for the dramatic bit. Cracked stone, old church, that sort of thing. Mostly what you want is somewhere that's been left alone a long time and had something happen to it once."

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "Prospecting mainly takes time, and a walk about. You'll turn up a patch or you won't. What you turn up depends on the ground round here and on how much of this you've done before - that's it, that's the whole system."

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "Patches come in grades. The better, the more room there is for a vein to grow, and create more calc. Barren ones you leave; nothing takes in them."

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "Different parts of London tend to skew more to a specific type. Round here it's whatever's going. Whitechapel's emotion, mostly. The City's fate, which probably isn't much of a surprise."
He does not tell you which of these facts is the important one. You get the sense this is on purpose.

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "Go on. Have a look about. I'll be here."
You spend the better part of an hour looking at brickwork with a seriousness that would embarrass you if anyone you knew walked past. Somewhere under all of it, London is doing what it does.
